title: A Spacecraft Flew Through the Sun's Atmosphere at 430,000 mph

scenes.text: A spacecraft flew through the Sun's atmosphere at 430,000 miles an hour.
scenes.keywords: sun surface solar flare close up

scenes.text: Christmas Eve 2024. NASA's Parker Solar Probe passed 3.8 million miles from the Sun's surface. Closer than anything ever built.
Its shield faced 2,500 degrees. Behind it, the instruments sat at a cosy 85.
That speed takes you from New York to Tokyo in under a minute. The fastest thing humans ever made.
The Sun's own gravity whips it faster on every pass. A slingshot.
430,000 miles an hour. And it phoned home.

description:
On 24 December 2024, NASA's Parker Solar Probe flew just 3.8 million miles from the Sun's surface at about 430,000 miles an hour, the closest and fastest any human-made object has ever gone.
Its carbon heat shield faces around 2,500 degrees Fahrenheit while the instruments behind it stay near 85 degrees. At that speed you could travel from New York to Tokyo in under a minute.
Would you volunteer for a one-way trip to the Sun? Comment below.
first_comment: The probe was out of contact for the whole flyby. NASA only knew it had survived when a beacon signal arrived two days later, on 26 December. What is the longest you have gone without your phone?
